questions.prompt: Talk the Talk — There’s a Method in My Madness. You have three methods for solving a system: graphing, substitution and linear combinations. For each method, choose when it is most appropriate.

responses.label: Graphing is most appropriate when…
options: both equations are easy to graph, as in slope-intercept form, and an estimate of the solution is enough.
you need an exact solution with fractions, because a graph shows every fraction exactly at the crossing.
one equation is already solved for a variable, because then the other line cannot be drawn.
a variable has opposite coefficients, because lines with opposite coefficients are easiest to draw.
responses.answer: both equations are easy to graph, as in slope-intercept form, and an estimate of the solution is enough.

responses.label: Substitution is most appropriate when…
options: one equation is already solved for a variable, or a variable has a coefficient of 1 or −1.
both equations are in standard form with large coefficients on every variable, like 7x + 9y = 4.
a variable has opposite coefficients, because substitution works by adding the equations.
you only need an estimate of the solution, because substitution gives approximate answers.
responses.answer: one equation is already solved for a variable, or a variable has a coefficient of 1 or −1.

responses.label: Linear combinations is most appropriate when…
options: both equations are in standard form and a variable’s coefficients are, or can be made, opposites.
one equation is already solved for y, because then neither equation needs to be multiplied.
the equations have no constant terms, because constants cannot be added together in a system.
you want to see where the two lines cross, because adding equations draws both lines at once.
responses.answer: both equations are in standard form and a variable’s coefficients are, or can be made, opposites.

responses.label: Which method is most efficient for 5x + 3y = 9 and 2x − 3y = 12?
options: Linear combinations — 3y and −3y are additive inverses, so adding the equations cancels y.
Substitution — x has a coefficient of 1 in one equation, so it is quick to isolate.
Graphing — both equations are in slope-intercept form, so each line is quick to draw by hand.
Substitution — both equations are already solved for y, so substitute right away.
responses.answer: Linear combinations — 3y and −3y are additive inverses, so adding the equations cancels y.

responses.label: Use the method you chose. The solution of 5x + 3y = 9 and 2x − 3y = 12 (x, y)

hints: Think about the form of each equation. What does each method need to get started?
Substitution starts by isolating a variable. When is that quick?
Linear combinations starts by making a pair of coefficients additive inverses. When are they already close?

reasoning: Graphing: easy to graph, shows the solution, but may only estimate it.
Substitution: one equation solved (or easy to solve) for a variable.
Linear combinations: standard form, with coefficients that are or can be made additive inverses. For 5x + 3y = 9 and 2x − 3y = 12, adding cancels y: 7x = 21, so x = 3, and 5(3) + 3y = 9 gives y = −2.
solutionReview.commonError: Choosing graphing for systems whose solution has fractions, where a graph only estimates it.
